discussion_comments.comment_body: `prepareHandoffRepository` isn't in `CLOUD_HUB_OPERATIONS` in #15205, so it won't be reachable through the Hub client. It's also called in both prepare and run (via `resolveCloudModel`), along with `loadCloudModels` and 8 `assertHandoffAccount` calls. Resolving once and carrying a scope token in the snapshot would remove most of the repeated checks.

The missing Hub operation is fixed: `prepareHandoffRepository` is registered in `CLOUD_HUB_OPERATIONS`, validated by the Hub service, and exposed by `CloudHubClient`. The preparation snapshot also captures a `CloudHubScope`, which subsequent operations carry so they cannot silently switch accounts. Socket coverage exercises repository preparation, and account-scope tests cover changes during recovery. This addresses the RPC compatibility issue; it does not remove the repeated model/repository checks.

The current implementation also removes the repeated preparation pass: `resolveCloudModel` runs during preview, and the approved snapshot retains the model, organization, and `CloudHubScope` for launch. `prepareHandoffRepository` is available through the merged Hub client. Account checks still surround asynchronous work so an old approval cannot launch under a different account.

Callers pass the name of a field as a string: `"statusWriteQueue"` or `"compactionStateWriteQueue"`. The call site does not say what the string does, and the compiler accepts the wrong string. This is the problem with a boolean parameter, one step removed. Please pass the getter and setter for the queue instead, or give each queue its own small method over one shared body.
Done: `enqueueStatusWrite` and `enqueueCompactionStateWrite` each hand a getter/setter pair for their queue to one `chainWrite`. No strings.

Similar to feedback on your other PR, I suggest using a string union here instead of a boolean. Booleans often are not flexible enough to model what is going on, and tend to proliferate. Then you get a lot of booleans where a subset of the states are invalid and it gets confusing and hard to test.

Not introduced here: queued follow-ups on `main` already echo the resolved prompt the same way (`queueToActiveSession` sends `resolvedPrompt` with `delivery: "queue"`, and `pending_prompt_submitted` carries whatever was enqueued). Out of scope for this PR — we'll fix it once for both paths separately.

Implemented in commit `84db143`.

The model-facing prompt and the user-facing prompt are now carried separately through the pending-input path. Mention resolution continues to produce the expanded prompt and attachment context used by the runtime, while the original answer is stored as `displayPrompt` on the pending entry and submitted event. The VS Code translator renders `displayPrompt`, so an answer such as `Use @/spec.txt` remains exactly that in the chat bubble and edit surface instead of exposing the resolved file content.

The regression now exercises a resolved prompt alongside the original display text and verifies that attachments remain attached to the displayed user feedback. The focused VS Code suites pass (231 tests total), the Core pending-prompt/host/Hub suites pass (152 tests), and the SDK typecheck passes.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Agreed, this one's worth closing in the PR: the hub now accepts `displayPrompt` on input, so it should carry it back out. @dakjdakd — could you forward `displayPrompt` in the two event copies (`session-event-projector.ts` `pending_prompt_submitted` case and `HubRuntimeHost`'s `session.pending_prompt_submitted` case)? No shipped host hits this path today, but a field that goes in and never comes out is a trap for the next integrator.

Fixed in e6dd0b4.

Both submitted-event copies now forward `displayPrompt`: the server's `pending_prompt_submitted` projection into the Hub envelope, and `HubRuntimeHost`'s conversion back into a Core event. The expanded model prompt, delivery mode, image/file arrays, and attachment count are preserved alongside the original display text.

The regression sends a Core submitted event through the real server projector and HubRuntimeHost event handler and checks both payloads. It covers a separate display string, an explicitly empty display string, and an omitted field. The Hub runtime, run-handler, and pending-prompt suites pass (58 tests), the SDK build and Core typecheck including smoke checks pass, and the changed files pass Biome.

This one is pre-existing and out of scope for this PR. The manifest handling lives in `UnifiedSessionPersistenceService.updateSession`, which this PR does not touch, and the behavior is the same on main. It is also not reachable from any product surface: the desktop sidebar runs the new name through `normalizeSessionTitle`, which turns an empty string into `undefined`, so a clear is never sent, and `cline history update` requires a non-empty `--title`. If we add a reset-to-auto-title affordance later, the fix is a one-line `delete manifestMeta.title` in the persistence service, but I would rather keep this PR to the hub transport bug it is fixing.
